summary: A trace can improve reconstruction while also increasing data exposure, storage cost and false confidence in reproducibility.

points.text: Prompts, tool outputs and environment snapshots can contain credentials, personal data and proprietary code. Capture-time redaction, retention limits and access control are part of the pattern, not optional cleanup.

Recording model settings and inputs does not make stochastic output bit-for-bit reproducible, and external systems may have changed. Re-execution must report divergence instead of claiming deterministic replay.
If the acting agent controls which events and evidence are emitted, the trace can omit failed attempts or side effects. The host must capture boundary events independently.
High-volume traces can become an unreadable second log platform. Stable schemas, sampling for low-value telemetry and a deliberately small evidence envelope are required.
